bib.title: RAG and RAU: A Survey on Retrieval-Augmented Language Model in Natural Language Processing

read.skipped: Reference list (from ~char 87500) skimmed only for lineage; Table 1-3 are flattened by extraction and only partly legible.

question: How can retrieval-augmented language models (RALMs), covering both generation (RAG) and understanding (RAU), be organised into a taxonomy of retrievers, language models, enhancements, data sources, applications and evaluations?
contributions: Covers RALM for both NLG (RAG) and NLU (RAU), not just RAG.
Describes Retriever and Language Model in detail and defines the interaction modes between them for the first time.
Gives an overview of the RALM work timeline, applications, limitations, proposed solutions and future directions.

results.claim: RALM is defined as y = F(x, z), with retrieved information z, input x, output y.
Survey names three retriever-LM interaction modes: sequential single, sequential multiple, parallel (interpolation).
results.setup: Parallel interaction, Eq. 5 (kNN-LM style interpolation with weight lambda)

limits: No experiments of its own; every result is reported from cited work, many without numbers or setups.
Authors concede four limitations: poor robustness, poor retrieval quality, overspending (cost of pretraining/finetuning and large retrieval stores), few applications.
Coverage ends around early 2024 (latest cited work); published v2 June 2025 but no later methods (agentic RAG, reasoning-RL retrieval) appear.
Tables 1-3 lack metrics; no comparative numbers across methods.
Text has some errors, e.g. RoBERTa/BERT citations swapped in Table 2 and Sec 4.1, and image/video dataset text repeated for audio.
practices: Choose interaction mode by task: single for simple QA, multiple (iterative/active) for long dialogue and multi-hop, parallel interpolation for kNN-LM style (Sec 2).
Use BM25 as a generalisable open-domain sparse retriever (Sec 3.1.1); dense dual-encoder (DPR, Contriever) is the common default (Sec 3.2).
Screen internet retrieval; rerank with BM25 or TF-IDF to cut noise (Sec 3.3, 9.2.2).
Control retrieval quality: filter, grade as correct/incorrect/ambiguous, fall back to web search (Sec 5.1.1).
Optimise retrieval timing: fixed stride, low-confidence tokens, CoT-triggered (Sec 5.1.2).
Use Fusion-in-Decoder to consume many passages (Sec 5.2.1).
Reduce cost with plug-and-play intermediate modules and in-context RALM, not model changes (Sec 9.2.3).
Evaluate with RAGAS, RGB, CRUD-RAG, ARES, MIRAGE, RECALL (Sec 8).

terms.definition: the process of refining the output of the LM with retrieved information to obtain a satisfactory result for the user
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (NLG tasks) and Retrieval-Augmented Understanding (NLU tasks), together RALM
retriever finds Top-K documents z for input x, then the LM generates from x and z
multiple retriever-LM rounds, LM generates and output is used for further retrieval when needed
retriever and LM work independently on x and outputs are combined by weighted interpolation
retriever enhancements: improve relevance of retrieved content; decide when to retrieve
